name: Amy Wyss
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Amy Wyss's father, Swiss billionaire Hansjoerg Wyss, founded medical equipment firm Synthes in the 1970s, where she worked for years.
Johnson & Johnson acquired Synthes in 2012 for $19.7 billion in cash and stock. Amy Wyss received a portion of the proceeds from the sale.
A 2014 U.S. Senate investigation into offshore tax evasion, which did not implicate the Wyss family, revealed her fortune.
She founded the LOR Foundation in 2007 to improve the quality of life for rural communities in the rural Mountain West.
forbes_facts: Wyss met her husband, Ed Jaramillo, on a chairlift in the Rockies.
Wyss is both an American and Swiss citizen.

name: Mehmet Ali Aydinlar
forbes_bio: Mehmet Ali Aydinlar is founder and leader of Turkey's largest chain of private hospitals, Acibadem Healthcare Group.
He began his career as a consultant for the hospital industry before starting Acidadem, which he took public in 2000.
Abraaj Capital joined him as a partner in 2008. Four years later Aydinlar brought on Malaysia's sovereign wealth fund and Kuala Lumpur-based IHH Healthcare Berhad, and the company was delisted.
Aydinlar exchanged Acibadem shares for cash and stock in IHH. He still owns 10% of Acibadem and serves as chairman of its board of directors.
Acibadem has been expanding into the Netherlands, Bulgaria, Macedonia and Serbia.
forbes_facts: Aydinlar has been buying real estate since his days as a consultant for hire. In 2019, he was named Entrepreneur of the Year in Turkey by Ernst & Young.
His primary philanthropic undertaking is Istanbul-based Acibadem University, whose mission is to advance healthcare in Turkey through education and research.

name: Habil Khorakiwala
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Pharma tycoon Habil Khorakiwala chairs Wockhardt, one of India's top makers of generic drugs.
He founded Wockhardt in 1967 after breaking away from his family's storied retailing empire.
His son Murtaza runs the Mumbai company which counts the U.K. as one of its top markets.
forbes_facts: His daughter Zahabiya oversees the hospital arm while another son heads the charitable foundation.
Khorakiwala has served as the honorary consul general of Sweden in India.

name: Todd McKinnon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Todd McKinnon is the cofounder and CEO of Okta, a cloud security company.
He previously served as a vice president at Salesforce, leaving in 2009 to found Okta.
When he left, he created a PowerPoint presentation for his wife explaining why the risk was worth it.

Okta took off during the Covid-19 pandemic, when demand for its identity and access management tools, including multi-factor authentication and access control, allowed thousands of clients' employees to access their work apps from anywhere.
McKinnon owns roughly 4% of the company, which went public in 2017.
forbes_facts: McKinnon got hooked on computers because his friend's dad owned a PC. McKinnon would write and dictate the pair's school papers, while his friend would type them.

name: Steven Schuurman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2024)
forbes_bio: Schuurman cofounded Elastic, a Netherlands-based software company that went public in 2018 on the NYSE.
Elastic creates software for search, data and analytics purposes.
Schuurman, who has a nearly 6% stake in Elastic, first became a billionaire in 2018.
He served as Elastic's CEO from 2012 to 2017, and still sits on its board of directors.
He cofounded another software company, SpringSource, which was acquired by VMware in 2009 for $420 million.
forbes_facts: Some of Schuurman's hobbies include cooking and playing guitar.
He also founded and chairs FutureNL, a non-profit that supports digital literacy in Dutch primary and secondary schools.

name: Jan-Hendrik Goldbeck
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Jan-Hendrik Goldbeck is co-CEO of the eponymous construction giant founded by his father  Ortwin Goldbeck in 1969.
Goldbeck's projects include factories, warehouses, schools, offices and residential properties.
The company, which employs 12,500 people, works on more than 500 projects annually.
Goldbeck and his brothers, Jörg-Uwe and Joachim, each own about a third of the company.

name: Wang Shuifu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Shuifu chairs equipment manufacturer Xizi Clean Energy Equipment.
Xizi Clean Energy was previously known as Hangzhou Boiler Group; Hangzhou Boiler went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2011.
Wang Shuifu started his career selling agricultural machinery in 1970.

name: Vidit Aatrey
forbes_bio: Vidit Aatrey is chairman, managing director and chief executive of Bangalore-based e-commerce firm Meesho.
He cofounded Meesho in 2015 with his college pal from IIT, Delhi.
Meesho is a shortened version of 'meri' ( the Hindi word for 'my') and shop.
Investors include Japan's SoftBank as well as private equity players such as Peak XV, Naspers Ventures and Elevation Capital.
The company got listed in December 2025.
forbes_facts: Before starting his own venture, Aatrey worked with tobacco giant ITC and Bangalore-based InMobi Technology Services.
